dishes.name: Andouille de Guéméné
dishes.desc: Smoked pork andouille from Guéméné-sur-Scorff in the Morbihan, built from rings of chitterling in layers. Served cold in slices or hot with potatoes and mustard.

dishes.name: Niniches de Quiberon
dishes.desc: Sucette-shaped salted-butter caramels from Quiberon and sold in paper bags. Found in sweet shops and markets all around Vannes and the Gulf.

dishes.name: Gâteau breton
dishes.desc: Dense, buttery shortbread-style cake made with salted butter, often with prune or apple filling, from Morbihan and Finistère. Baked in bakeries around Vannes and Carnac.

dishes.name: Sardines de Quiberon
dishes.desc: Sardines from Quiberon, the Morbihan's canning town, sold fresh in season or tinned in vintage-labelled boxes. Quiberon's canneries date from the 19th century.

dishes.name: Gulf of Morbihan oysters
dishes.desc: Oysters farmed in the sheltered Gulf of Morbihan and the Quiberon bay. Eaten raw at oyster stalls and on the quays around Vannes, Auray and Locmariaquer.
